issues.explanationEnglish: 'demi-petit pain' is unnatural French. The Spanish 'tostada' inside the French gloss also leaves the toast itself unexplained.
issues.proposedFrench: la media (tartine grillée sur un demi-pain)

issues.explanationEnglish: Same structure as card 1. It should use a French gloss with a natural noun phrase.
issues.proposedFrench: la entera (tartine grillée sur un pain entier)

issues.explanationEnglish: False equivalent. French 'pain viennois' is a soft, milk-enriched bread. Reader 6 describes the Andalusian pan de viena as having a thin, crunchy crust, so 'de type viennois' points French readers to the wrong bread. Keep the Vienna reference without evoking pain viennois.
issues.proposedFrench: le pan de viena (petit pain dit « de Vienne »)

issues.explanationEnglish: 'saindoux de porc' is redundant, since saindoux is already pork fat. 'au paprika' adds a detail that is not in the English gloss. Pork can stay explicit with a more natural phrase.
issues.proposedFrench: la manteca colorá (saindoux de porc rouge à tartiner)

issues.explanationEnglish: The adjective is merged into the headword. The target is the noun 'mie', and the English gloss is an explanation of it.
issues.proposedFrench: la mie (l'intérieur moelleux du pain)

issues.explanationEnglish: False equivalent. In everyday French, 'grillage' means wire mesh or fencing. Its toasting sense is rare and reads oddly.
issues.proposedFrench: le degré de grillé (à quel point le pain est grillé)

issues.explanationEnglish: 'une demie' / 'une entière' turns menu labels into generic French words. 'une demie' usually suggests a half-hour or a half-pint. Cards 1–2 teach media/entera as labels, so keep them. The phrasing is also more natural with 'selon qu'on a plus ou moins faim'.
issues.proposedFrench: Ici, on commande une media ou une entera, selon qu'on a plus ou moins faim.

issues.explanationEnglish: Perspective drift. The Spanish uses 'tú' ('pides'), and the reader version uses 'tu'. The card switches to generic 'on'.
issues.proposedFrench: Si tu commandes un mollete, le pain reste moelleux à l'intérieur.

issues.explanationEnglish: The Spanish imperative 'pide' (direct advice) becomes a generic statement with 'on commande'. This changes the speech act and does not match reader 4. Keep the label 'entera'.
issues.proposedFrench: Si tu as très faim, commande une entera.

issues.explanationEnglish: The imperative 'evita' becomes a generic 'on évite', which weakens the direct pork warning and does not match reader 15.
issues.proposedFrench: Si tu ne manges pas de porc, évite la manteca colorá et la zurrapa.

issues.explanationEnglish: The card uses guillemets and inline glosses, while cards 16–19 do not. The glosses also clutter a short question. 'o de viena' can stay elliptical, as in the Spanish.
issues.proposedFrench: Excusez-moi, le pan de la casa, c'est un mollete ou du pan de viena ?

issues.explanationEnglish: 'corrigé' assigns a masculine gender to an unspecified speaker, while the Spanish is gender-neutral. 'je ne le savais pas' is also stiffer than the usual 'je ne savais pas'.
issues.proposedFrench: Merci pour la correction, je ne savais pas.

issues.explanationEnglish: 'une demie' has the same label problem as card 16. 'avec tomate et huile' without articles is also clunky.
issues.proposedFrench: Pour moi, une media tomate-huile, s'il vous plaît.

issues.explanationEnglish: 'une demie / une entière' has the same label problem as card 16.
issues.proposedFrench: Moi : « Ici, on commande une media ou une entera, selon la faim que tu as. »

issues.explanationEnglish: Keep the label 'entera' consistent with cards 2 and 18.
issues.proposedFrench: Moi : « Si tu as très faim, commande une entera. »

issues.explanationEnglish: The gloss 'moelleux' is immediately repeated by 'reste moelleux'. Drop the gloss here because the sentence itself explains the bread.
issues.proposedFrench: Moi : « Si tu commandes un mollete, le pain reste moelleux à l'intérieur, parce qu'il a beaucoup de mie. »

issues.explanationEnglish: The gloss 'de type viennois' makes the same false equivalent as card 4. Here it also contradicts the 'thin, crunchy crust' described in the same sentence.
issues.proposedFrench: Moi : « Le pan de viena (petit pain dit « de Vienne ») a une croûte plus fine et plus croustillante, et beaucoup de gens le préfèrent pour ça. »

issues.explanationEnglish: 'un petit pain plus petit' is redundant and awkward after the gloss 'petit pain'.
issues.proposedFrench: Moi : « Si tu commandes un pitufo, on t'apporte un pain plus petit, parfait pour accompagner un café. »

issues.explanationEnglish: Same gender assumption as card 21. The narrator's gender is unspecified in the source.
issues.proposedFrench: Moi : « Merci pour la correction, je ne savais pas. »

issues.explanationEnglish: The glosses duplicate the definitions that the sentence itself gives, as in 'manteca colorá (saindoux de porc au paprika) est du saindoux de porc au paprika'. Drop them. 'saindoux' alone already means pork fat, but keeping 'de porc' once is fine for the pork point.
issues.proposedFrench: Moi : « La manteca colorá, c'est du saindoux de porc au paprika, et la zurrapa de lomo contient de petits morceaux de longe de porc dans du saindoux. »

issues.explanationEnglish: The indirect object is missing. Spanish 'le explico' means 'je lui explique', and bare 'j'explique' is incomplete in context.
issues.proposedFrench: Ingrid me dit qu'elle ne mange pas de porc, et je lui explique que le jamón serrano (jambon cru espagnol) est aussi du porc.

issues.explanationEnglish: This line has three problems. (1) 'grillage léger' uses the same false equivalent as card 14. (2) 'On commande avec' has no object and is unnatural. (3) Register drift: Spanish 'se la sacamos' uses the usted/third-person 'se', and Rocío is serving a customer, but 'te' makes her informal.
issues.proposedFrench: Rocío : « Vous la demandez peu grillée, et on vous la sert plus moelleuse. »

issues.explanationEnglish: 'une demie' has the same label problem. 'avec tomate et huile' without articles is clunky.
issues.proposedFrench: À la fin, Ingrid commande une media tomate-huile, peu grillée, et Rocío lui laisse la salière sur la table.

summaryEnglish: The scene, names (Ingrid, Rocío, Triana, Séville) and pork facts are preserved, and most of the French reads naturally. Main problems: (1) 'grillage' for 'tueste' is a false equivalent and should be replaced with 'peu grillé' / 'degré de grillé' (cards 14, reader 17). (2) 'pain de type viennois' wrongly points to French pain viennois and contradicts the crunchy crust in reader 6. (3) 'une demie / une entière' should keep the taught labels media/entera. (4) The cards switch from tú-advice and imperatives to generic 'on' (cards 17–19). (5) Rocío's 'te' breaks the formal 'se/usted' register. (6) 'j'explique' is missing 'lui'. (7) Reader 7 says 'petit pain plus petit', and reader 13 repeats its definitions in the glosses. (8) 'corrigé' assumes a male narrator. Guillemets are used inconsistently between cards 16–19 and 20–23.
